findings.claim: The gy=121 ORACLE frame's blit call list IS reachable+capturable on the patched trace core (prior findings said it was not). A fresh drive settles at gy=118 (at the gate), then forward steps walk 118->119->120->121 freely (the door at gy=123 is the first block). Serializing gy=121 on the patched core round-trips fine. Capturing at ega.drv FUN_0a93 over an IN-PLACE redraw (turn left then right back to facing 0 — NOT a forward step, which would walk the party off the cell mid-trace) yields a REPRODUCIBLE (byte-identical x2) 31-call list: 4 masked (near side-panel mirror pairs, all OR-merge) + 27 OR (forward blits, incl. the pre-mirrored right-half placements 134/138/162/166/.. and the 6 destRow-7 top strips 346/349/352/355/358/361). Composing it (composeBackground + applyMaskedMirror over mazedata.ega) reproduces 99.909% of the gy=121 oracle viewport.

findings.claim: The 99.909% residual is 18 viewport px / 26 page bytes, all in the deep-door-center detail (page plane0/2/3 at bx19..20, y68..76 — the door leaf at the corridor vanishing point). This detail is NOT representable by adding ANY of the 366 static mazedata.ega placements: an exhaustive sweep of every single OR addition, every masked self-OR / self-REPLACE, every masked pair (i->j, j->i) over the door-region candidates, and every skip/REPLACE of an existing captured call FAILS to reduce the page-region diff below 26 bytes (most increase it). So the deep-door detail is drawn by a path BEYOND the OR/masked background blit (FUN_0a93) — likely a runtime-clipped door piece or a separate door-leaf draw — not yet reversed.

findings.claim: The 366 mazedata.ega placement records are organized into DEPTH BANKS that the wmaze view loop indexes per depth. The perspective ceiling strips are placements 122/123/124/125 (destRow 32/39/51/59 = depths 0/1/2/3), the floor mirror at 150/151/152/153 (destRow 128/104/88/83, = 122+28..125+28), the corner/door-frame pieces at 133/137/141/145 (stride 4) and their +28 floor twins 161/165/169/173, and the 6 destRow-7 top strips at 346/349/352/355/358/361 (stride 3). The masked-mirror PAIRS swap a left/right side panel (e.g. 19<->15 = img7<->img3, the w4 h112 full-depth side walls). The near-frame REPLACE void-carve pieces are 23..34 (img11..22). This banked structure is consistent across the gy=118 (60-call) and gy=121 (31-call) captures, and is the visible analogue of the wall-span depth emit. BUT the exact (depth -> bank base + per-slot index) arithmetic is NOT pinned: it lives in the slot helpers (wmaze 0x3828/0x3c11/0x3dce + the 0x4892 cluster) which Ghidra's decompiler fails on (overlay control-flow), and a static-disasm read of the index math was not byte-confirmed this pass.

findings.claim: The gy=118 and gy=121 frames produce GENUINELY DIFFERENT call lists (cross-check that the law is geometry-dependent, not a single hardcode). gy=118 (at the gate, N-wall code 2 at the current cell, door code 3 at depth 2): 60 calls = 26 masked (18 OR-merge perspective mirrors + 8 REPLACE void carves) + 30 OR + 4 trailing masked REPLACE — the door renders LARGE/CLOSE. gy=121 (open, door code 3 still at depth 2 but 3 cells of open corridor first): 31 calls = 4 masked + 27 OR — the door renders SMALL/FAR. Composing gy=118's captured list against the gy=121 oracle = 48.47% (confirming they are different frames, not the same scene). The depth profile of forward-edge codes (facing-0 forwardEdge = N(cell at gy+d)) is gy=118 [2,0,3,0] vs gy=121 [0,0,3,0] — the door is at the same map cell (gy=123) but a different rendered DEPTH because the party moved 3 cells closer-to-far.
